item.title: graalvm-ce: generate cacerts from cacert
item.description:
Part of #576543.

GraalVM CE, graalvmPackages.graalvm-ce, is a binary JDK with a bundled Java trust store, lib/security/cacerts. This trust store has 111 certificates, and 33 of them are not in cacert. This change makes a new cacerts with 118 certificates from the cacert bundle with jre-generate-cacerts, as the merged openjdk change #576518 does. The change uses the keytool of the package, and autoPatchelf must patch this keytool before it can operate. Thus, the change sets dontAutoPatchelf = true, and postFixup does autoPatchelf before it makes the new cacerts. graalvm-oracle uses the same buildGraalvm.nix, but the harness did not examine graalvm-oracle.

item.title: rubyPackages.certified: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA file
item.description:
Part of #576541.

The certified gem has a bundled CA file, certs/ca-bundle.crt. The last version of the gem is 1.0.0 from 2014-07-19, thus this file is from 2014, and no newer version is available. The only function of the gem is to make Net::HTTP use the CA file of the gem. This change adds a certified entry in pkgs/development/ruby-modules/gem-config/default.nix, which replaces the file with a symlink to the ca-bundle.crt file of cacert in postInstall. After this change, that file is the cacert bundle, thus on nixpkgs the gem makes Net::HTTP use cacert, the same decision as for python3Packages.certifi.

In nixpkgs, rubyPackages.kramdown-rfc2629 and the Ruby environment of Discourse include this gem. kramdown-rfc2629 does require 'certified' only when it cannot open the default CA file of OpenSSL and the default CA directory has no PEM files. The Gemfile of Discourse has the gem with require: false, and only the tests of Discourse do require "certified", in spec/rails_helper.rb. The change applies to all software that does require "certified". The open pull request #577131 changes the same file for four other gems, and it adds the same cacert argument at the same position. git merge-file merges the two changes with no merge conflict.

item.title: python3Packages.raven: use cacert bundle instead of vendored CA file
item.description:
Part of #576541.

raven has a bundled CA file, raven/data/cacert.pem. raven uses this file for HTTPS connections when it cannot import certifi. This change replaces the installed file with a symlink to the ca-bundle.crt file of cacert in postFixup. Thus, the installed file is a symlink to cacert, and replaceDependencies can replace cacert. The wheel in the dist output keeps the bundled file (#576542).

item.title: gam: use cacert bundle for the vendored fallback CA file
item.description:

item.title: temurin-bin: generate cacerts from cacert
item.description:
Part of #576543.

Heads up, most of this change is a reindent – you can press "hide whitespace" in the diff to make it easier to read.

The Temurin binary JDKs, temurin-bin and temurin-jre-bin, have a bundled Java trust store, lib/security/cacerts. This change makes a new cacerts from the cacert bundle with jre-generate-cacerts, as the merged openjdk change #576518 does. temurin-bin is also the bootstrap JDK of openjdk. Thus, this change adds the argument regenerateCacerts, and openjdk sets it to false for its bootstrap JDK. The drvPath of each openjdk does not change. This change does not change jmods/java.base.jmod or the darwin packages.

The JDKs semeru-bin and semeru-jre-bin also come from temurin-bin/jdk-linux-base.nix. At this time, their JVM does not start on nixpkgs, and it shows this error: cannot enable executable stack as shared object requires: Invalid argument. This occurs because glibc 2.41 and newer versions do not accept a library that must have an executable stack, and libj9vm29.so is such a library. Thus, it is not possible to use keytool at build time. This change sets regenerateCacerts = false for these two packages, and their drvPath does not change. The repair of these two packages (a new version, or meta.broken) is a different task.
